subject.title: fix(clickclack): recover when API requests stall

question: Should ClickClack control-plane REST calls now fail after 30 seconds without response headers or a body chunk, while multipart uploads remain governed by transport progress timeouts?
rationale: The code and tests can establish the mechanics, but only maintainers can set the supported latency policy for existing ClickClack servers and reverse-proxy deployments.

options.title: Accept the bounded control-plane budget
options.body: Approve the 30-second header and body-idle limits as the supported failure-recovery contract, preserving the upload exemption.

options.title: Choose different timeout semantics
options.body: Specify a different documented budget or an explicit configuration path if supported deployments need longer control-plane waits.

options.title: Pause for deployment evidence
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers can confirm the intended behavior against representative ClickClack and reverse-proxy deployments.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded control-plane budget
recommendation.body: Approve the 30-second header and body-idle limits as the supported failure-recovery contract, preserving the upload exemption.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current timeout implementation and can incorporate the outcome, though a current-main area owner should make the policy choice.
